pr_title: Change RSA.LegalKeySizes for Apple platforms to return 8192
pr_body:
This changes RSA.LegalKeySizes to return a maximum of 8192 on Apple platforms, as opposed to 16384. At least on macOS Sequoia and Sonoma, the limit is 8192-bit.

While we are here, memoize the `KeySizes` instance. They are immutable. The returned array is not - so we only memoize the interior `KeySizes` instance, not the returned array.

Closes #110588.
pr_comments: Should we add a test that keys with the max size can be created?

> Should we add a test that keys with the max size can be created?

We do here

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/cc66c7769902766ccdf26af708f4484d04e3e604/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/Security/Cryptography/AlgorithmImplementations/RSA/KeyGeneration.cs#L23-L27

But it's (effectively) a manual-only because it takes about ~30 seconds for macOS to generate an RSA 8K key. It can take several minutes for platforms that support 16K keys. Even for Outerloop that's too long, in my opinion.

This manual-only test fails without the fix, which is what prompted me to make the change.

issue_context.title: macOS: RSA.Create and Import fails with > 8192-bit keys
issue_context.body:

```C#
RSA rsa = RSA.Create(16_384);
rsa.ExportParameters(true);
```

I don't think it really matters one way or the other if 16K keys work (they are obscenely large) however, the MaxKeySize is `16_384`

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f377332dfd3ebe0b36631d37c1e555eece1bc9bb/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Security/Cryptography/RSASecurityTransforms.cs#L50

Since I don't see a way to get a 16K key to work with Apple platforms, we should probably just lower this to 8192, which does appear to work, as recently as macOS 15.1.1.

We have a test for 16K keys that fails, but it is guarded by "IsStressModeEnabled".

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/cc66c7769902766ccdf26af708f4484d04e3e604/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/Security/Cryptography/AlgorithmImplementations/RSA/KeyGeneration.cs#L23-L27

It fails when I do `DOTNET_TEST_STRESS=true ./dotnet.sh test src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/tests --filter GenerateMaxKey`, so I guess we never run with this enabled on macOS.

review_comments: could this limit be higher in certain configurations like someone installed something and now they can use 16k or i.e. different limit on mobile etc? Just curious if 16k wasn't made because one of those allows it

As far as I can tell there is no way to use a 16K key with SecurityTransforms. If I had to guess, .NET originally supported 16K keys on macOS in .NET Core 1.x days when crypto on macOS was build on OpenSSL and we just kind of assumed that didn't change when we ported to Apple's Security framework.

while this looks correct, we seem to use [CloneKeySizesArray](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f6e46ff86b784db1106e2148d84e43432f96116c/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Security/Cryptography/KeySizeHelpers.cs#L12) elsewhere - this will make potential down-porting easier

It doesn't really make sense to use it here for me, and we don't use it in RSABCrypt.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/95814d0f99fd876fdc2f6b5b4cf5d5fc94adaea9/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/RSABCrypt.cs#L355

Using `CloseKeySizesArray` would mean memoizing an array as well, so it would just mean more things unnecessarily held as a static.

It does make sense to use it for EC algorithms since they cannot have their key sizes represented as a single instance of `KeySizes`.
